pages.title: 07 — Subqueries & CTEs — Complete Reference (1)
pages.text: Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3d63906c5d6c81b3827dd00cea7f2845 as of 2026-09-09T13:39:47.762Z: {"title":"07 — Subqueries & CTEs — Complete Reference (1)"} null ## Purpose Canonical home for SQL subqueries and Common Table Expressions (CTEs), with emphasis on grain, scope, correlation, execution behavior, readability, and choosing the right pattern. ## 1. Core Mental Model A subquery is a query nested inside another query. The important question is not merely where it appears, but what shape it returns and how the outer query consumes it. Think in four shapes: - Scalar → one value - Single-column list → many values from one column - Derived table → rows and columns used as a relation - Correlated subquery → evaluated logically in relation to the current outer row ## 2. Subquery in WHERE Use when the business question is about membership or existence. ```sql SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN ( SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE order_date >= DATE '2026-01-01' ); ``` ### IN vs EXISTS - IN expresses membership in a returned set. - EXISTS expresses whether at least one matching row exists. - For anti-matching, prefer NOT EXISTS when NULL behavior could make NOT IN unsafe. ## 3. Scalar Subquery in SELECT A scalar subquery returns one value per outer row. ```sql SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, (SELECT MAX(o.order_date) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id) AS last_order_date FROM customers c; ``` Use it when the relationship is naturally one value per outer row. If the logic becomes complex or expensive, consider a JOIN or pre-aggregation. ## 4. Derived Tables A subquery in FROM becomes a temporary relational result for the outer query. ```sql SELECT customer_id, total_sales FROM ( SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_sales FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id ) s WHERE total_sales > 100000; ``` This is especially useful when you must aggregate first, then filter or join. ## 5. Correlated Subqueries A correlated subquery references columns from the outer query. ```sql SELECT c.customer_id FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.amount > 10000 ); ``` The key idea is row-relative logic: the inner condition depends on the current outer row. ## 6. Nested Subqueries A nested subquery contains another subquery. Nesting is valid, but deep nesting can hide business intent. Prefer a CTE or staged transformation when each logical step deserves a name. ## 7. CTEs A CTE names an intermediate query using WITH. ```sql WITH customer_sales AS ( SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_sales FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id ) SELECT * FROM customer_sales WHERE total_sales > 100000; ``` CTEs improve readability, decomposition, reuse within a statement, and debugging. They are primarily a query-organization mechanism; do not assume a CTE automatically materializes or improves performance in every database. ## 8. Multiple CTEs Use sequential CTEs when the analytical problem has clear stages. ```sql WITH monthly_sales AS ( SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, customer_id, SUM(amount) AS sales FROM orders GROUP BY 1, 2 ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY month ORDER BY sales DESC) AS rnk FROM monthly_sales ) SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 10; ``` ## 9. Subquery vs CTE vs JOIN vs Window Function | Technique | Best fit | | --- | --- | | JOIN | Bring related attributes/rows together | | EXISTS | Test whether a related row exists | | IN | Membership in a set | | Scalar subquery | One value per outer row | | Derived table | Transform rows before outer query | | CTE | Name and stage complex logic | | Window function | Compare a row with related rows without collapsing grain | ## 10. Grain Is the Deciding Factor Before writing the query, state the grain. Example: - Source grain: one row per order line. - Required result: one row per customer. If you aggregate inside a subquery/CTE before joining to customers, you can control row multiplication and preserve the intended grain. ## 11. Real BI Use Case — Student Analytics Business question: Which students are currently active and have completed more credits than the average active student? ```sql WITH active_students AS ( SELECT student_id, earned_hours FROM enrollment_snapshot WHERE status_code = 'ACTIVE' ), avg_hours AS ( SELECT AVG(earned_hours) AS avg_earned_hours FROM active_students ) SELECT s.student_id, s.earned_hours FROM active_students s CROSS JOIN avg_hours a WHERE s.earned_hours > a.avg_earned_hours; ``` The CTE separates population definition from benchmark calculation, making the logic easier to validate. ## 12. Correctness Checks Before trusting a subquery/CTE solution: 1. What is the outer-query grain? 2. What shape does the inner query return? 3. Can the inner query return multiple rows where a scalar is expected? 4. Can NULL change the result of IN / NOT IN? 5. Will a JOIN be clearer or safer? 6. Does the transformation accidentally multiply rows? 7. Can each stage be validated independently? ## 13. Performance Notes - Reduce rows early when appropriate. - Pre-aggregate before joining when the target grain is higher than the source grain. - Use execution plans rather than assuming a CTE/subquery is faster. - Correlated logic can be elegant but should be measured on large datasets. - Index/filter columns that participate in selective predicates and joins where appropriate. ## 14. Interview Traps - A CTE is not automatically a temporary table. - A CTE is not automatically faster than an equivalent subquery. - EXISTS checks existence; it does not need to return the matching values. - A scalar subquery must logically produce at most one value for each outer row. - NOT IN can behave unexpectedly when the subquery contains NULL. - DISTINCT should not be used as a blind fix for row multiplication. ## 15. Canonical Ownership This page is the single canonical reference for Subqueries and CTEs. Legacy pages should preserve useful examples and applied material, but should point back here for the complete conceptual treatment.
